evidence.why: Auth token and user id are taken directly from the untrusted protocol link and forwarded to the renderer with no independent server-side verification step before being treated as authentication data.

evidence.snippet: const token = params.get('token'); const userId = params.get('user');
evidence.why: Link-supplied token/user values are passed on (protocol:auth IPC) as if authoritative, letting an external link drive authentication state without server verification.
Routing is based on attacker-controlled host/path/params with no schema validation beyond simple string checks, and params are passed through largely unchecked to renderer handlers.

controls_present: fixed switch-based host routing (closed set of cases)
other_classes_observed: sensitive token logged/forwarded without secure channel
no CSRF/replay protection on auth params
